title: Vickers Wellington T2834
memorial_details:
Dark grey marble stone on a plinth of local Ancaster stone depicting at top a Vickers Wellington twin engined bomber approaching head on and slightly nose down. Badges of the RAAF and RCAF are engraved bottom left and right.

The memorial was erected by Lillian Brindley, indicating a local connection and impact.

A dark grey marble stone on an Ancaster stone plinth was erected near the crash site, bearing the badges of the RCAF and RAAF and a poem composed by Lillian Brindley, who erected the memorial.
inscription: IN MEMORY OF/ PILOT OFFICER HENRY ERIC 'HARRY' RATH R.C.A.F./ AND/ SERGEANT KARL MORRIS MIEGEL R.A.A.F./ WHO DIED WHEN THEIR VICKERS WELLINGTON (T2834)/ CRASHED NEAR HERE IN THE EARLY HOURS OF/ MONDAY 20th APRIL 1942/ MY ROSE/ The most perfect rose that I ever knew,/ Began from a seed and gradually grew.../ That rose is the love that blossomed in me,/ For someone who died that we may be free/ How treasured they are/ Precious memories like those,/ A priceless gift, my perfect rose./ Lillian Brindley
narrative: In the early hours of Monday 20 April 1942, Vickers Wellington T2834 crashed near North Rauceby in Lincolnshire. Pilot Officer Henry Eric 'Harry' Rath of the Royal Canadian Air Force and Sergeant Karl Morris Miegel of the Royal Australian Air Force were both killed.
original_title: Pilot Officer H E Rath and Sergeant K M Miegel
community_connection: The memorial was erected by Lillian Brindley.
